name: --add-dir
description: Allow file access to an additional directory and load its trusted .github/skills and .github/agents configuration.

examples.explanation: Allow a sibling library and load its trusted Copilot agent and skill definitions.

when_to_use: Use when a task legitimately spans another trusted directory.
when_not_to_use: Do not add an untrusted directory because its agent and skill configuration may be loaded.

name: --additional-mcp-config
description: Add or override MCP servers for one session using an inline JSON value or an @-prefixed file path.

examples.explanation: Add project-specific MCP servers without changing the user's persistent file.

when_to_use: Use for temporary MCP servers or automation-specific overrides.
when_not_to_use: Use the persistent MCP configuration for servers needed in every session.

name: --agent
description: Start the invocation using a named custom agent.

examples.explanation: Start with the configured security-reviewer agent.

when_to_use: Use when a task should use one custom agent's tools, prompt, and configuration from the outset.

conditions: The named custom agent must be available and trusted.

name: --allow-all
description: Enable all tool, path, and URL permissions for the invocation.

examples.explanation: Run a programmatic task inside a separately controlled disposable environment.

when_to_use: Use only in a trusted, appropriately isolated execution environment.
when_not_to_use: Do not use on untrusted repositories or where narrower allow rules are sufficient.

conditions: Equivalent to allow-all-tools, allow-all-paths, and allow-all-urls; managed policy can disable bypass permissions.

name: --deny-tool
description: Deny a tool or scoped permission pattern; deny rules take precedence over allow rules.

examples.explanation: Allow Git commands except git push.

when_to_use: Use to carve explicit high-risk exceptions out of broader allow rules.

name: --effort
description: Set the reasoning effort for the selected model when the model supports configurable effort.

examples.explanation: Request higher reasoning effort for a difficult design review.

when_to_use: Use when a supported model should spend more or less reasoning effort on the task.
when_not_to_use: Do not assume every model supports every effort value.

conditions: Supported levels depend on the selected model.

name: --output-format
description: Select plain text or JSON Lines output for the invocation.

examples.explanation: Return JSON Lines suitable for a consuming program.

when_to_use: Use JSON when programmatic consumers need structured event output.

name: --prompt
description: Execute one prompt programmatically and exit after pending task handling and the final result.
when_to_use: Use in scripts, CI, or shell pipelines where an interactive session is not appropriate.
when_not_to_use: Use interactive mode when the task requires ongoing clarification or approval.

name: --resume
description: Open the session picker or resume a session by exact name, identifier, or identifier prefix.

examples.explanation: Choose a session from the interactive picker.
Resume an exactly named session directly.

when_to_use: Use when returning to prior work whose conversation and task history should be preserved.

conditions: Bare --resume requires a TTY when multiple sessions exist and conflicts with --continue.

name: --sandbox
description: Enable the operating-system shell sandbox for the current session without changing the saved setting.

examples.explanation: Run a headless tool-using task with the OS-level sandbox enabled.

when_to_use: Use to opt one session into stronger shell isolation.

name: --stream
description: Enable or disable progressive display of Copilot responses.

examples.explanation: Wait for a complete response instead of rendering it progressively.

when_to_use: Disable streaming when a consuming terminal or harness should receive the completed response as one result.

name: --worktree
description: Create or reuse an isolated Git worktree under a sibling .worktrees directory and start the session there.

examples.explanation: Create or reuse an isolated auth-refactor worktree.

when_to_use: Use to isolate concurrent changes or an experimental implementation from the current checkout.
when_not_to_use: Do not combine it with resume, continue, or connect session selection.

conditions: Only available in experimental mode and requires a Git repository.
